STUDENT STORIES ON VIDEO

Student Transformation on Video

Watch real classroom cases of student guidance in short videos.

※ All student names are pseudonyms.

CASE 1Guiding a Student Through Smartphone Overdependence

This video shows how a student struggling with smartphone overdependence builds self-control and changes his behavior through “phone check-in” practice with his teacher.

CASE 2Resolving a Student Conflict Through a Teacher’s Apology and Active Listening

This video shows a teacher who first apologizes for judging too quickly after hearing only one side, then listens to both students—helping them recognize their own mistakes and reconcile.

CASE 3A Frequently Late Student Changes Morning Habits Through Home–School Collaboration

This video shows a teacher sharing with a student’s mother how frequent lateness can affect peer trust and the child’s self-esteem, and how home and school work together to help the student build an on-time morning routine.

CASE 4A Student Who Cried Over Losing Learns to Accept the Result Through Teacher–Parent Collaboration

This video shows a student who used to cry after losing a game learning to manage his feelings and accept the result. With patient support from his teacher and mother, he comes to realize that the joy of playing with friends matters more than winning.

STUDENTS

How value-centered character education changed students

Students who take value standards as their guide in life help, respect and care for one another, and live positively and vibrantly, each with their own gifts.

※ All student names are pseudonyms.

“Youngchan, you’re doing so well lately!”Understanding and forgiveness between friends

When Youngchan, who had drifted away from friends, tried hard to be considerate, the teacher asked the class for understanding and forgiveness. At recess, classmates were the first to pat Youngchan on the shoulder with praise, and everyone laughed together.

A child who lost friends through anger
“I can’t control it on my own yet”The power to judge without being told

Jungwoo, who was often late because of gaming, agreed to hand in the phone for a week. Even after the promise ended, Jungwoo kept handing it in, and by the second semester could manage alone.

A child overly immersed in gaming
“Teacher, I held back my anger today!”Changes in friendships and emotions

Mina, who came alone to the teacher almost every period, gradually began coming with friends and a brighter face, and grew into a child who held back anger and kept promises to a younger sibling.

A child dependent through lack of affection
A child who brightened by helping othersA life changed by the value of love

Onyu, a class president who had only taken care of their own work, began helping friends with cleaning after learning the value standard of love. A once-dark face that avoided eye contact brightened, and classmates nominated Onyu for a good-deed award and as a leader.

A once self-centered child
CLASSROOM CASES

How questions and empathy changed classrooms

※ All student names are pseudonyms.

Honesty chosen with a red pencil

Case 1 · Jinsu, 4th grade

The situation
After the final exam, Jinsu brought an answer sheet claiming it had been marked wrong, but the answer, originally 1, had been changed to 4.
What the teacher did
The teacher talked with Jinsu quietly after the other students left. When Jinsu stayed silent, the teacher didn’t press, handed over a red pencil so Jinsu could mark the answer, and waited.
What changed
Jinsu crossed out the answer, choosing honesty, and left with a proud, bright face. It never happened again.
The conversation

Teacher:Jinsu, mark it yourself. A circle if it’s right, a cross if it’s wrong. A score you get by cheating isn’t your real ability. I hope you make the brave choice that lets you stand tall.

(A moment later, Jinsu brings back the answer sheet with a cross on it.)

Teacher:Thank you for choosing honesty. Being honest makes you feel proud and at ease, doesn’t it?

Student:(smiling brightly) Yes.

A lie is a lie, even as a joke

Case 2 · Cheolsu, after a fight with a friend

The situation
Cheolsu told a lie as a joke. When Youngsu called Cheolsu a “liar,” a fight broke out, and Cheolsu blamed Youngsu.
What the teacher did
Instead of lecturing, the teacher used the 3S (3-Step) Questioning Method, following up with “Why isn’t it right?” and “Who would it hurt?”
What changed
Cheolsu realized that lying harms not only friends but also oneself, and decided what to do from now on.
The conversation

Teacher:Cheolsu, is lying right, or not right?

Student:It’s not right.

Teacher:Why isn’t it right? Who would it hurt?

Student:Youngsu… and it’s not good for me either. It can start a fight.

Teacher:So what would be good to do from now on?

Student:I shouldn’t lie, even as a joke.

The real reason, heard by asking instead of scolding

Case 3 · Beomsu, 6th grade

The situation
Beomsu kept bringing a toy puppy and playing with it in class, even after being told for over a month not to. Asked why, Beomsu sat silent, head down, for 20 minutes.
What the teacher did
The teacher reflected on having asked like an interrogation, and made it clear the question came from real curiosity, not from wanting to scold.
What changed
Beomsu finally shared what was inside, promised to keep the toy in the bag during class, and brightened up.
The conversation

Teacher:Beomsu, you usually don’t bring things you’re told not to, but you keep bringing this one. I’m not trying to scold you. I’m really curious.

Student:This toy is like my little brother.

Teacher:Do you feel anxious without it?

Student:Yes.

Teacher:Then how about keeping it in your bag and not taking it out during class?

Student:(face brightening) Okay!

TEACHER VOICES

How teachers’ happy reflection changes classrooms

What teachers said after our teacher training.

These classroom stories might encourage another teacher.

```
